instructions.about: Fill this file from a modal (finite-element) solve so the Sound Microscope (analyze.html#modal) can play it. Fields named 'instructions', 'source' and 'figure.spec' are ignored by the page; keep or delete them.
steps: 1. Solve the natural modes of the part or assembly (e.g. CalculiX *FREQUENCY, Abaqus, COMSOL, Ansys) with mass-normalised mode shapes phi (phi^T M phi = 1).
2. Pick the listening point p (for a pickup: the tine tip, in the pickup's direction) and one or more strike points s.

3. For every mode i: f = frequency in Hz; m_i = 1 / phi_i(p)^2; E_i = 0.5 * m_i * (2*pi*f)^2 * d^2 with d = reference.deformation_mm / 1000; w_i = phi_i(s) / phi_i(p), signed, one value per strike id.
4. Leave out modes where phi(p) is close to 0: they are silent at the pickup.
5. Optionally give each mode its own T60 in seconds (from measurement or assumed modal damping zeta: T60 = 6.91 / (zeta * 2*pi*f)). Modes without T60 use the two damping knobs.
6. Mark the mode that is the played note with "fundamental": true.
7. Render the figure described in figure.spec from the STEP file, save it next to this file, and put its path (relative to analyze.html) or a data: URI in figure.src.
8. Drop the file on the lab in chapter 8, or use import .json.
instructions.units: f Hz · E J · w dimensionless · T60 s · impulse mN·s · contact ms · deformation mm

reference.point: pickup point, e.g. tine tip, vertical

strikes.label: near strike, e.g. 6 mm from the clamp
reference strike used for the default sound
far strike, e.g. 24 mm from the clamp

figure.alt: Isometric view of the part, with arrows at each strike point
figure.caption: Where the hammer strikes. Distances measured from the clamp face.

spec.purpose: One explanatory drawing of the simulated part, generated from its STEP file, showing what was modelled and where each strike point is. Same style as data/rhodes_N30_D3.webp.
spec.canvas: 2000 x 1200 px, landscape 5:3, WebP or PNG, under 300 kB. Flat background #ececea, no border, no shadow under the model.
spec.view: True isometric projection of the STEP geometry, seen slightly from below and in front so the struck face is visible. Model fills the middle ~70 % of the width, leaving room for callouts. No perspective.
spec.shading: Flat light-grey solids (#d6d6d2 lit faces, #bdbdb9 side faces, thin #9a9a96 edges). Rubber parts (grommets, felt) near-black #2b2b2b. The part that vibrates and is struck (tine, bar, string) darkest, #3a3a3a. Fasteners and springs mid grey with visible coils. Fixed parts may be slightly transparent to show hidden screws.
spec.kicker: Top left at x=70, y=75: part name, note and assembly in IBM Plex Mono 400, 22 px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.06em, #6d6d6a, items separated by ' · '. Example: RHODES N30 · D3 · TONE BAR ASSEMBLY.
spec.title: Below the kicker at y=145: 'where the hammer strikes' in Archivo 700 (or Inter Bold), 64 px, #111111, lowercase, tight letter-spacing -0.02em.
spec.callouts: One per main part: IBM Plex Mono 400, 18 px, UPPERCASE, #222222, with a straight 1.5 px #222222 leader line from the label to the part. Add key dimensions after ' · ' (e.g. 'TINE · 84.9 mm', 'TONE BAR · 156 mm, slot + 90° twist'). Mark fixed boundaries '(fixed)'. Labels outside the model, never crossing it.
spec.datum: A dotted 1.5 px #222222 line at the zero of the strike distances, labelled in mono 18 px lowercase, e.g. 'block face = 0', with a thin dimension line along the struck part.
spec.strikes: One vertical arrow per strike id, pushing on the struck face in the hammer direction, 4 px shaft, solid triangular head, round dot at the contact point. Colours from strikes[].color: secondary #6d6d6a, default #ff4f00, tertiary #3a5fc4. Under each arrow its distance in IBM Plex Mono 20 px in the arrow colour; the default strike's label 500 weight and slightly larger. Arrows may be staggered in length so labels do not overlap.
spec.pickup: Optional: a 2 px #ff4f00 ring at the listening (reference) point, labelled 'pickup · reference point' in mono 16 px.
spec.footer: Bottom left at y=1110: two lines of Archivo 600, 22 px, #111111 that say what pushes where and which strike is the reference (this text also goes in figure.caption). Bottom right: 'isometric · not to scale for arrows' in IBM Plex Mono 400, 18 px, #6d6d6a.
spec.accessibility: Write figure.alt as a full sentence listing the parts and the strike positions, for readers who cannot see the image.
